people: Liu Song prince in Northern Wei

claims.event: Clerk who urged Liu Huaizhen to purge stray gods from the Yao temple, joined the Founder at Huaiyin, urged the dynastic name Qi, and memorialized on schools, thrift, law, music and rewards.
Inspector who, on Cui Zusi’s word, cleared stray gods from the Yao temple.
Sage ruler whose temple held stray gods; cited as a model of thrift.
Rebel whose image as Lord Su stood in the Yao temple; Cui Zusi called him a fifth Evil.
The Founder, joined by Cui Zusi at Huaiyin, who took the dynastic name Qi on his advice.
Han ruler cited for frugality.
Consort of Emperor Wen whose skirts did not sweep the floor.
Cast coin from tent-hook bronze.
Married off a daughter with only a black tent and ten maids.
Mocked for rinsed rice, cited as frugal.
Liu Song founder praised as surpassingly thrifty.
Consort of Emperor Wu of Song whose room had only blue silk nets.
Urged Emperor Wu of Song to keep musicians.
Ancient ruler cited for plainness.
Han minister who on leaving Qi entrusted only prisons and markets.
Han official who said the Qin’s surviving failure was its prison officers.
Han legal-family member cited as a model lineage.
Han legal-family member cited as a model lineage.
Ancient dragon-keeper whose transmitted craft is cited.
Han minister who proposed dismissing 441 Grand Music performers.

label.en: Senior Staff Officer of the Chancellor-of-State
Acting Gentleman-in-Attendance of the Yellow Gate

claims.event: Memorialist on farming, history-writing, remonstrance and worthies; made Champion General on the Huai and inspector of Qing and Ji, mourned by the emperor at his early death.
Ancient ruler who drew on heaven’s stores against the flood.
Ancient ruler who overcame drought through allotted fields.
Upright scribe of antiquity cited by Cui Zusi.
Censor of old cited by Cui Zusi.
Censor of old cited by Cui Zusi.
Han Commandant of Justice held up as a model.
Called up by Han as Remonstrance Grandee.
Blunt Han official imprisoned and later restored.
Worthy drawn to Yan by the honoring of Guo Wei.
Trusted friend through whom Guan Zhong was found.
Ruler who trusted Bao Shuya and gained Guan Zhong.
Minister (Yiwu) obtained through Bao Shuya.
Kinsman of Cui Zusi who fought for the Founder at Xinting, defended Zhongli, and sent raids across the Huai; posthumously Rear General, named Xiangzi.
Inspector of Xu who rebelled in Taishi and killed Liu Mizhi.
Rebel whose rising Cui Wenzhong helped resist.
Army commander sent by Cui Wenzhong to storm Chamazhi.
Northern garrison chief of Chamazhi, killed.
Northern Yangping administrator, killed.
Northern Guantao magistrate, killed.
Northern Puyang magistrate, killed.
Administrator of Matou killed by the northerners.
Army commander sent against Bai Zhongdu.
Northern Zhuyi garrison chief, killed.
Army commander sent against Liang E.
Northern Huaiyang administrator, killed.
Huaibei loyalist who routed the northerners at Baodugu.
Pingyuan man who fed the starving in Qingzhou, broke out to Beihai in the Taishi revolt, and governed Jizhou and Hailing.
General Who Guards the North, clan elder cousin of Liu Shanming.
Father of Liu Shanming, Song administrator of Qi and Beihai.
Ruler who marveled at Liu Shanming’s blunt answers.
Inspector of Qing who joined Xue Andu’s revolt and later surrendered.
Paternal uncle of Liu Shanming who deceived Shen Wenxiu, turned loyal at Xiapi, and was killed by Xue Andu.
Army commander sent by Shen Wenxiu to aid Xue Andu.
Clan elder cousin of Liu Shanming who rallied Bohai for the court, inspector of Jizhou.
Ruler who posthumously honored Liu Mizhi.
Paternal kinsman of Liu Shanming (rendered "Huaimin" in the translation) who held Beihai commandery for the court.

label.en: Consultative Officer to the Rapid Cavalry General
Left Leader of the Crown Prince

claims.event: Mourned his captive mother until Tian Huishao ransomed her, pledged himself to the Grand Ancestor, foresaw Shen Youzhi’s failure, became Baron of Xingan, and submitted an eleven-point memorial.
Ruler who sighed with pity at Liu Shanming’s grief.
Beiping townsman named by Liu Shanming as envoy north, who ransomed his mother.
Cousin of Liu Shanming who led troops to the sea islands, served the Grand Ancestor as secret observer and messenger.
Song prince on whose pacifying-army staff Liu Sengfu served.
Cruel Song ruler later deposed.
Administrator of Donghai whom the Grand Ancestor hoped would stir the northerners.
Rebel whose failure Liu Shanming predicted.
Earlier rebel who collapsed without a battle.
Earlier rebel cited as defying heaven.
Named by Liu Shanming as a root of the revolt.
Named by Liu Shanming as a root of the revolt.
Han strategist to whom the Grand Ancestor compared Liu Shanming.
Han strategist to whom the Grand Ancestor compared Liu Shanming.
Minister of Works who urged Liu Shanming not to retire.
Predecessor whom Liu Shanming replaced in Huainan.
Song prince in the north cited as a lingering threat.
Ancient ruler cited as a model.
Ancient ruler cited as a model.

label.en: Acting Inspector of Qing and Ji
Consultative Officer to the Rapid Cavalry General
Right Marshal to the Grand Commandant
Staff Officer to the Prince of Ancheng’s Pacifying Army

claims.event: Frugal remonstrator who halted the Xuanyang Gate, wrote to Cui Zusi, died in Jianyuan 2 at 49 leaving 8,000 scrolls; posthumously Left General, Earl Lie.
Youthful friend of Liu Shanming, then inspector of Qing and Ji.
Rebel whose armies threatened the capital; later broken with Zhang Yong.
Hoisted by rival factions against the throne.
Hoisted by rival factions against the throne.
Son and heir of Liu Shanming whose household received grain from the Grand Ancestor.
Cousin of Liu Shanming, Front General and Baron of Fengyang, died governing Baxi and Zitong.
Wuyi man who served Xue Andu, fled south, became the Grand Ancestor’s trusted registrar at Huaiyin.
Grandfather of Su Kan, administrator of the home commandery.
Rebel who took Su Kan onto his staff and later defected north.
The Lord who held Huaiyin, employed Su Kan, and wrote the Ballad of the Frontier Guest.
Song general whose defeat lost Huaibei.

label.en: Staff Aide in charge of Records

claims.event: Envoy and recorder for the Grand Ancestor, co-author of Records of Grand Marshal Xiao, Marquis of Xinjian; died Jianyuan 1 at 53, posthumously Marquis Zhi.
Baxi man who rebelled early in Yuanhui.
The Sovereign whom Su Kan and Yuan Rongzu served, called Lord Xiao by Chu Yuan.
Rebel whose rising led to Su Kan’s promotion.
Co-compiler with Su Kan of Records of Grand Marshal Xiao.
Younger brother of Su Kan, Baron of Jiyang, inspector of Ba, died administrator of Chenliu.
Garrison commander on whose staff Su Lie served.
Rebel against whom Su Lie defended the city.
Xiapi horseman and slinger, served Xue Andu then the Grand Ancestor, Viscount of Jiangle, inspector of Yan.
Minister of the Five Armaments, younger cousin of Yuan Rongzu.
Warlord cited by Rongzu as a model of arms and letters.
Wei ruler cited by Rongzu alongside Cao Cao.
Cousin of Yuan Rongzu, administrator of Huaiyang, exiled and killed by Emperor Xiaowu.
Inspector of Yu, uncle of Rongzu, starved himself after his son was exiled.
Song ruler who exiled and ordered the killing of Yuan Xizu.
Song ruler at whose accession the realm revolted.
Inspector of Xu who detained Rongzu and led the northerners into Pengcheng.
Vicegerent to whom the Grand Ancestor recommended Rongzu.
Song ruler whose removal preceded Rongzu’s promotions.
Townsman of Rongzu who ferried his arms chest north.
Townsman of Rongzu who ferried his arms chest north.

label.en: Director of the Feathered Forest Guard
Recorder on the Southern Pacification Staff
General Who Prances like a Dragon
Consultative Officer to the Rapid Cavalry General
Inspector of Liang and South Qin

claims.event: Advised wording that blamed Liu Yin rather than the Prince of Badong; died Yongming 9 at 57.
Prince of Badong denounced as a rebel by frontier commanders.
Official blamed by Rongzu for harrying the Prince of Badong.
Uncle of Rongzu, held Liang Mountain against Yixuan, defeated Xue Daobiao, died Yongming 5 at 76, posthumously Ding.
Ruler who posted Yuan Hong to Xuyi.
Rebel defeated by Yuan Hong.
Prince who shared palace duty with Yuan Hong.
Cousin of Rongzu, valiant-cavalry general, plotted against Pei Zulong, executed after joining Yao Guang’s revolt.
Rebel who made his son-in-law Pei Zulong administrator of Xiapi.
Son-in-law of Xue Andu, administrator of Xiapi.
Prince of Shi’an whose revolt Lisheng joined.
Han counselor whose words Liu Shanming’s advice is compared to.
Praised for serving the hidden ascent.

label.en: General Who Prances like a Dragon
Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon
Right Leader of the Heir Apparent
